title: In a first, US will allow some private firms to carry out cyberattacks
headline_summary: US reverses decades-old ban, allows private firms offensive cyberattacks
blurb: The US is sweeping away decades of cybersecurity policy that previously banned private companies from conducting offensive cyberattacks and 'hack back' operations. The new executive order now permits select private firms to legally execute these operations independently. This regulatory shift opens new market opportunities for security startups pursuing offensive capabilities and reshapes venture investor appetite for cyber operations.

title: Morgan Stanley's infrastructure partner Zerohash rebuffed in pitch to be U.S. trust bank
headline_summary: Zerohash rebuffed in bid for U.S. trust bank status
blurb: Zerohash, an infrastructure partner to Morgan Stanley in the crypto space, applied to become a U.S. trust bank and was rebuffed by regulators. The denial illustrates how skeptical U.S. authorities remain toward crypto-native financial firms seeking banking status. For VCs investing in fintech and crypto infrastructure, it highlights a critical bottleneck: regulatory approval remains inaccessible even for well-connected crypto companies.

title: SEC clears Franklin Templeton funds to use onchain BENJI system for cash management
headline_summary: SEC clears Franklin Templeton for onchain BENJI cash management
blurb: Franklin Templeton obtained an SEC no-action letter enabling its traditional registered investment funds to directly invest in BENJI/FOBXX, an onchain cash settlement and management system. The approval opens the door for institutional capital to flow into blockchain infrastructure. For crypto investors and founders, this represents proof that SEC regulators will greenlight crypto-native financial services—a critical signal for industry legitimacy.

title: SEC Staff Clears Franklin Funds to Use Onchain Money Fund for Cash and Collateral
headline_summary: SEC approves Franklin Templeton onchain money fund for institutional use
blurb: The SEC staff approved Franklin Templeton's registered funds to hold FOBXX, its onchain money market fund, subject to 12 custody and control conditions. This relief lets asset managers integrate blockchain infrastructure into their institutional cash management and collateral operations. The approval removes regulatory friction for onchain money markets and creates clearer pathways for traditional finance to adopt blockchain-based settlement rails.

title: SEC Advances Tokenized-Securities Exemption That Could Enable 24/7 Trading
headline_summary: SEC advances tokenized-securities exemption for 24/7 onchain trading
blurb: The SEC advanced a tokenized-securities exemption enabling 24/7 onchain trading. The framework permits compliant blockchain securities trading while broader regulatory rules are developed in parallel; Friday's scheduled Commission vote includes a separate offering proposal. This regulatory move matters significantly: VC-backed fintech and crypto infrastructure startups have been waiting for this clarity to build continuous, permissioned capital markets without traditional market hours.

title: BitGo CFO to Exit as Q2 Net Loss Hits $19 Million
headline_summary: BitGo CFO exits amid $19M quarterly loss
blurb: BitGo's CFO is exiting the cryptocurrency custody platform amid a $19 million Q2 net loss. Revenue grew 80% year-over-year, but trading and staking margins compressed, forcing the company to cut $15 million in annualized costs following June layoffs. The CFO departure signals margin pressures in crypto infrastructure—strong revenue growth doesn't guarantee profitability.

title: Brad Lightcap Leaves OpenAI After Eight Years as It Prepares for an IPO
headline_summary: Brad Lightcap exits OpenAI as company eyes IPO
blurb: Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's CFO and COO for eight years, is leaving to start an undisclosed venture. His exit marks another senior departure from the company as it prepares a potential IPO, following a run of executive exits this year. Losing a seasoned financial operator during the critical pre-public phase creates execution risk and tests OpenAI's operational readiness ahead of market debut.

title: Ex-LocalGlobe trio plots new VC firm
headline_summary: LocalGlobe trio launches independent venture fund
blurb: Three veteran partners are departing LocalGlobe to launch an independent venture capital fund targeting European early-stage technology companies. The trio brings decades of combined investing experience and plans to continue their proven investment thesis while operating with full autonomy. This departure reflects mounting consolidation pressure within traditional European VC structures and signals rising founder appetite for nimble, independent, partner-led investment vehicles.

title: Longtime OpenAI executive Brad Lightcap leaves as shake-up at AI lab continues
headline_summary: Brad Lightcap exits OpenAI amid ongoing leadership changes
blurb: Brad Lightcap, a longtime executive at OpenAI, is departing the company. His exit marks another departure in an ongoing series of leadership changes at the AI lab, signaling internal shifts. For VCs tracking governance and talent flows at major AI companies, executive departures often signal strategic restructuring, capital reallocation decisions, or operational pivots—follow-on hires reveal the strategic direction.

title: OpenAI’s head of ethics leaves less than a year after joining
headline_summary: OpenAI ethics leader exits after less than a year
blurb: OpenAI's head of ethics departed after serving less than a year in the role. The departure raises questions about governance priorities and internal alignment at one of the world's most influential and closely-watched AI labs. For VCs tracking OpenAI's valuation and direction, leadership exits at this level expose cultural or strategic friction within a high-stakes, heavily-funded asset.

title: Some Simple Economics of Open versus Closed AI
headline_summary: Who funds AI when open weights are free?
blurb: A16z analyzes the core economic question plaguing AI: who funds and secures models when open weights are free? If trained model weights become commodities, funding responsibility and safety accountability become murky. This tension directly shapes venture allocation decisions between open-source infrastructure plays, proprietary AI companies hunting defensibility, and the capital-intensive foundation bets that increasingly demand premium valuations to survive competition.

title: Databricks closed a $5B funding round at a $190B valuation, six months after raising $5B at a $134B valuation, and says it has crossed $7B in revenue run rate (Samantha Subin/CNBC)
headline_summary: Databricks raises $5B at $190B valuation, up 42% in six months
blurb: Databricks closed a $5 billion funding round at $190 billion valuation. The data lakehouse company raised this capital at a 42% higher valuation than its previous $134 billion round six months ago, and now reports $7 billion in annual revenue run rate. The rapid repricing signals sustained institutional conviction in AI infrastructure and validates Databricks' position as a clear category leader.

title: Kalshi in talks with Sequoia, Wellington for $750 million fund raise at $40 billion valuation
headline_summary: Kalshi targets $750M at $40B from Sequoia, Wellington
blurb: Kalshi is in talks to raise $750 million from Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management at a $40 billion valuation. The event derivatives platform operates prediction markets where traders can bet on real-world outcomes like elections and weather. The funding round signals strong institutional backing for blockchain-based prediction markets, a space that has attracted capital despite regulatory questions around event wagering.

title: Memory maker CXMT overtakes Tencent to become China's most valuable company 17 days after its IPO — now worth $524 billion
headline_summary: Memory chip maker CXMT becomes China's most valuable firm post-IPO
blurb: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) surpassed Tencent to become China's most valuable company 17 days after its IPO. The memory chip maker reached a $524 billion valuation, indicating strong investor appetite for domestic semiconductor manufacturers. The rapid ascent reflects Beijing's push for chip self-sufficiency and signals substantial capital flowing into strategic technology independence.

title: Report: Kalshi seeks $40B valuation, Sequoia and Wellington eye lead investor role
headline_summary: Kalshi targets $40B valuation with Sequoia, Wellington backing
blurb: Kalshi, a prominent retail prediction market platform, is raising fresh capital at a roughly $40B valuation. Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management are in talks to co-lead the funding round, representing substantial institutional confidence in the sector. The valuation reflects growing investor conviction that prediction markets and derivatives infrastructure represent a major fintech category, despite ongoing regulatory uncertainty in the space.

title: Legora in talks to raise at a $10bn valuation, according to reports
headline_summary: Legora in talks to raise at $10bn valuation
blurb: Legora is raising capital at a $10bn valuation, marking a significant funding milestone. The company has attracted strong investor interest at this price point, signaling robust market confidence and continued venture capital deployment into high-growth startups. For VCs and LPs, this round demonstrates successful scaling and competitive positioning, representing an important marker in the venture capital landscape and valuation trends.

title: Report: Swedish legal tech Legora in talks to double its valuation to $10B
headline_summary: Swedish legal tech Legora talks to $10B valuation
blurb: Legora, a Swedish legal tech startup founded by Max Junestrand in 2023, is in talks to double its valuation to $10B. The company provides automation tools for law firms and was built by founders with no legal background. The valuation jump signals European legal tech maturing, and that institutional capital is flowing to specialized B2B enterprise solutions beyond trendy AI and crypto plays.

title: CodeRabbit lands $143M at $1.5B valuation as AI-generated code surges
headline_summary: CodeRabbit raises $143M at $1.5B as AI code review surges
blurb: CodeRabbit raised $143M at $1.5B valuation, hitting unicorn status as AI code-review demand explodes. Investors backing the round are betting that AI-generated code will reshape how developers work and collaborate. This capital deployment signals that AI-powered developer tools are becoming foundational infrastructure—the kind of category-defining bet VCs make when they're confident it will anchor the next decade of software engineering.

title: Heaviside raises $60M at a $600M valuation, up 21x in three months
headline_summary: Heaviside raises $60M at $600M valuation in three months
blurb: Heaviside Industries closed a $60 million funding round at a $600 million post-money valuation. Three months ago the company barely existed publicly, but achieved 21x valuation growth, demonstrating intense investor enthusiasm for emerging players in hot spaces. The funding signals the velocity and capital deployment patterns in high-momentum sectors that VCs are evaluating as leading indicators of market direction.

title: Cerebras stock plunges 14% after second earnings report following IPO
headline_summary: Cerebras stock plunges 14% despite beating Q2 expectations
blurb: Cerebras Systems stock cratered 14% following its Q2 earnings report, the company's second since going public. The AI semiconductor chip maker delivered better-than-expected revenue and raised full-year guidance. Yet investors sold sharply, signaling deep concerns about profitability timelines for AI infrastructure companies.

title: Qunnect, Monarch partner on compact quantum networking hardware
headline_summary: Qunnect and Monarch partner on compact quantum networking hardware
blurb: Qunnect and Monarch are partnering to build smaller, manufacturable versions of Qunnect's Carina entanglement distribution system for broad quantum networking deployment. The collaboration directly targets the production-scale bottleneck: compact, integrated quantum networking hardware that commercial operators can actually manufacture and deploy. This partnership enables progress on a critical constraint in quantum infrastructure: manufacturing and deploying laboratory-scale quantum networking systems at commercial volumes.

title: AI coding startup Cognition reportedly already in talks to raise at $40B valuation
headline_summary: Cognition eyes $40B in mega-round just months later
blurb: Cognition is in talks to raise at $40 billion, just months after closing a $1 billion round at $26 billion. The AI coding startup's repricing represents a 54% increase and reflects intense competitive mega-round dynamics in autonomous coding. For VCs, this signals rapid consolidation—winners climb fast to mega-cap status, early backers face dilution pressure, and portfolio velocity accelerates.

title: Lovable confirms new $13.3B valuation, raises another $400M
headline_summary: Lovable confirms $13.3B valuation, raises $400M on $500M ARR
blurb: Lovable raised $400 million at a $13.3 billion valuation, positioning itself among the most valuable developer tools platforms. The AI coding assistant startup hit $500 million annualized run rate revenue in June, demonstrating strong customer adoption and unit economics. The funding underscores sustained investor confidence in AI-powered developer tools, showing the market rewards companies with proven scale, profitability metrics, and retention data despite rising competition from tech giants and specialized competitors.

title: CoreWeave proves Nvidia's aging AI GPUs from 2020 can generate profit nine years after deployment, signs A100 contracts into 2029 — power constraints and legacy infrastructure keep old GPUs profitable
headline_summary: CoreWeave hits $2.58B quarterly revenue on aging Nvidia GPU strength
blurb: CoreWeave reported $2.58B in quarterly revenue, up 112% year over year. The GPU infrastructure startup proves Nvidia A100s from 2020 still generate profit, with customer contracts locked through 2029. For VCs tracking AI infrastructure, this signals explosive demand for compute capacity and validates a durable business model even as chip supply tightens and individual GPUs age.

title: Lovable raises $400m backed by EU’s Scaleup Fund
headline_summary: Lovable raises $400M from EU's Scaleup Fund
blurb: Lovable raised $400 million in a funding round backed by the EU's Scaleup Fund, a public-backed European venture vehicle. The deal signals sustained capital appetite for European startups at scale and demonstrates regional fund maturity. Larger check sizes from EU-backed sources to individual companies mark intensifying competition for proven European founders and accelerating capital concentration in the region's startup ecosystem.

title: Drone startup Uforce targeting upwards of $4bn valuation in new raise, sources say
headline_summary: Drone startup Uforce targets $4bn valuation in funding round
blurb: Uforce, a drone hardware startup, is targeting a $4 billion valuation in its latest funding round, according to sources. The raise signals sustained investor appetite for autonomous robotics and commercial drone infrastructure platforms at scale. Valuations at this level indicate venture capital is consolidating behind deeptech companies demonstrating sustainable unit economics and defensible market positions in emerging autonomous systems categories.

title: Vibe-Coding Startup Lovable Hits $13 Billion Valuation
headline_summary: European AI startup Lovable valued at $13 billion
blurb: Lovable, an AI-powered platform for software development, reached a $13 billion valuation through a new funding round, catapulting the European startup into the ranks of Europe's most valuable companies. The company's achievement reflects strong investor appetite for European AI infrastructure and generative AI tools targeting developers. For VCs, this signals sustained capital flowing to European founders, demonstrates meaningful market demand for AI-native development solutions, and underscores Europe's emerging ability to scale AI startups to unicorn status.

title: World's largest sovereign wealth fund posts record $184 billion profit as it reveals SpaceX stake for the first time
headline_summary: Sovereign wealth fund posts $184B profit, reveals SpaceX stake
blurb: Norway's sovereign wealth fund posted a record $184 billion profit and disclosed its SpaceX investment stake to the public for the first time. The $2.34 trillion Government Pension Fund Global holds positions in 7,000+ companies across 60 countries globally. The SpaceX disclosure is rare and signals strong institutional confidence in deep tech; it also provides a market signal for private space company valuations.

title: A Founder’s Guide to the Secondary Market in 2026
headline_summary: Secondary equity sales become founder's main payout before IPO
blurb: Secondary equity sales—where founders and employees sell shares before IPO—have become the primary liquidity mechanism in venture. Secondary funds, crossover investors, and late-stage VCs now actively participate in these transactions, fragmenting what were traditionally acquisition exit paths. This restructures when LPs realize returns, reduces founder urgency to sell the company, and signals private company lifecycles are fundamentally longer.

title: 5 Interesting Learnings from Palo Alto Networks at $11.4 Billion in Revenue: 60% ARR Growth, 120% NRR, and a $25B Acquisition That Doubled the Stock
headline_summary: Palo Alto Networks hits $265B valuation on $29B acquisition spree, doubles stock
blurb: Palo Alto Networks deployed $29B in acquisitions over twelve months and doubled its stock price, now at a $265B market cap. ARR grew 60%, net retention hit 120%, and the stock hit an all-time high of $368.80. Shows how public SaaS consolidators extract outsized returns through M&A, not organic growth alone.

title: Intel Prices $20 Billion Stock Sale at $95, Below Monday's Close
headline_summary: Intel raises $20B to salvage foundry business
blurb: Intel priced a $20 billion stock offering at $95 per share, upsizing from the $15 billion announced Monday. The company declined to detail capital deployment. Its external foundry business—meant to compete with TSMC and Samsung—generated only $293 million in revenue last quarter. The raise signals Intel's desperation to reclaim chip manufacturing leadership amid collapsing market position.

title: HSBC Asset Management invests in London-founded Model ML
headline_summary: HSBC Asset Management invests in London fintech AI startup
blurb: HSBC Asset Management made an equity investment in Model ML, a London-founded startup building AI automation tools for financial services. The company was founded by two brothers and serves institutional finance operations. The investment signals traditional asset managers increasingly diversifying into direct venture capital allocation in AI and fintech, creating new and emerging competition for startup funding.

title: Robinhood Private-Market Fund Prices $200 Million IPO
headline_summary: Robinhood prices $200M private-market fund IPO
blurb: Robinhood priced a $200 million IPO for its private-market fund, RVII, expanding retail access to alternatives. The fund structure mirrors traditional GPs: 2% annual base fees and 20% carry on realized gains, with some exposure through illiquid vehicles. This signals retail brokerages now competing directly for LP capital in private markets, a sector historically reserved for institutional allocators and dedicated alternatives firms.

title: Josh Kushner raised $2bn to buy the companies AI is coming for
headline_summary: Kushner raises $2bn to buy and transform services firms with AI
blurb: Josh Kushner's Thrive Holdings closed a $2bn fund to acquire accounting and IT services firms and transform them with AI-powered workflows. The strategy inverts the typical AI business model: rather than selling tools to customers, Kushner buys the customer businesses outright, deploys his engineers inside, and rebuilds operations with AI. This targets services companies vulnerable to AI disruption by making them acquisition targets instead.

title: CodeRabbit raised $143m to read the code AI wrote
headline_summary: CodeRabbit raised $143M for AI code review automation
blurb: CodeRabbit is building AI-powered code review automation for development teams. The startup raised $143 million to address a critical bottleneck: as developers increasingly use AI coding assistants to write production code, manual peer review slows shipping velocity. The platform automatically reviews AI-generated changes for bugs and security issues, enabling faster deployment cycles for engineering teams scaling AI-assisted development practices.

title: Accel raised $3.5bn. Europe now gets the same fund as the US
headline_summary: Accel raises $3.5bn for four new funds; Europe gets same vehicle as US
blurb: Accel raised $3.5bn for four new funds serving US and European venture markets. The firm, which backed Atlassian, CrowdStrike, Flipkart, and Slack since 1983, now structures its Europe fund identically to the US version, giving LPs in both markets the same vehicle terms. Geographic parity enables Accel to compete for larger institutional commitments and establishes confidence in European venture returns.

title: Josh Kushner’s Thrive Holdings raises $2B at a $12B valuation to turn AI into a private equity strategy
headline_summary: Thrive Holdings closes $2B fund to embed AI in private equity strategy
blurb: Thrive Holdings closed a $2B fund at a $12B valuation to deploy AI systems across deal sourcing, underwriting, and active portfolio management. Josh Kushner's venture and private equity firm treats AI as core operating infrastructure for capital deployment, not a sector bet. This demonstrates how top VC and PE firms are now embedding artificial intelligence into their fundamental deal-making and allocation processes.

title: Accel raises $800m for ninth early-stage Europe fund
headline_summary: Accel closes $800m ninth early-stage Europe fund
blurb: Accel closed its ninth early-stage fund dedicated to European investment at $800 million in capital. The venture firm continues its strategy of raising region-focused vehicles to back European founders at seed and Series A stages. For LPs allocating to European early-stage, Accel's ability to consistently raise large funds signals sustained confidence in the firm's deal flow and execution.

title: Monzo and Lovable backer Accel raises enlarged $800M early-stage fund
headline_summary: Accel raises $800M early-stage fund for Europe and Israel
blurb: Accel raised an $800M early-stage fund focused on Europe and Israel, marking a significantly enlarged investment capacity in the region. The venture firm has previously backed prominent startups including Lovable, Synthesia, and Monzo, demonstrating strong portfolio depth across AI and fintech. This fund signals sustained LP confidence in early-stage European tech and confirms robust capital availability for founders navigating the current market.

title: Nvidia’s $500B AI investment pool could impact enterprise chip pricing, availability
headline_summary: Nvidia partners on $500B credit pool for enterprise AI chip purchases
blurb: Nvidia and six financial partners created a $500B investment pool to finance enterprise AI chip purchases on credit for customers. The consortium—Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR—targets frontier AI labs, AI cloud providers, and broader enterprise customers seeking infrastructure. The pool signals massive infrastructure demand growth but analysts warn it will exacerbate chip shortages and increase enterprise AI infrastructure costs.

title: Accel closes oversubscribed $550M India fund within weeks, 19 months after its last
headline_summary: Accel closes oversubscribed $550M India fund in weeks
blurb: Accel closed a $550M India fund, significantly oversubscribed within weeks. The new fund comes just 19 months after Accel's prior $650M India vehicle, which still retains 55% of its capital undeployed. The rapid fundraising signals strong LP appetite for India tech despite the firm's substantial existing dry powder, underscoring fierce competition among global VCs racing to secure emerging-market allocation ahead of peers.

title: What’s Scaleup Europe, the $5.7B fund that just backed satellite company ICEYE?
headline_summary: Scaleup Europe's $5.7B fund backs Finnish satellite firm ICEYE
blurb: Scaleup Europe, a $5.7B public-private fund, deployed its first investment into ICEYE, the Finnish Earth-imaging satellite company. The move marks the fund's transition from launch announcements into active capital deployment across European deeptech. For VCs, this establishes a significant new institutional competitor for space and satellite deals and signals how European public capital is concentrating in hardware and space.

title: The VC Firm That Helped Build Latin America’s Startup Scene Is Crossing Into Silicon Valley
headline_summary: Monashees, Latin American VC, opens permanent Silicon Valley office
blurb: Monashees, one of Latin America's oldest and most influential VC firms, opened a San Francisco office to establish permanent Silicon Valley presence. The firm believes regional startups increasingly need direct Silicon Valley access, strong networks, and capital to scale globally—especially as AI reshapes startup playbooks. This expansion signals a broader trend: Latin American VCs moving upstream to support portfolio companies through growth and compete with global investors.

title: Accelerant, which uses data analytics to connect insurance underwriters with risk capital partners, agrees to go private with Thoma Bravo in a $4.4B deal (Katherine Hamilton/Wall Street Journal)
headline_summary: Accelerant goes private with Thoma Bravo in $4.4B deal
blurb: Accelerant, which uses data analytics to connect insurance underwriters with risk capital partners, is being acquired by private equity firm Thoma Bravo for $4.4 billion. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027. The deal signals strong PE demand for technology-enabled insurance infrastructure and demonstrates a clear exit path for venture-backed insurtech platforms.

title: CXMT overtakes Tencent to become the most valuable Chinese company, with a ~$524B market cap, above Tencent's ~$510B; CXMT's Shanghai shares jumped 460%+ at IPO (Bloomberg)
headline_summary: CXMT's 460% IPO surge makes it China's most valuable company
blurb: CXMT's Shanghai IPO shares jumped 460%+ on debut, reaching a $524B market valuation in one trading session. The newly public company now surpasses Tencent Holdings ($510B) as China's most valuable public company. The dramatic pop signals the IPO market is hot for Chinese mega-cap tech and that fundraising windows remain open for large-cap companies despite geopolitical pressures.

title: Sources: Anthropic's investors expect it to float at a $2T+ valuation in an October IPO and to hit $100B to $120B in annualized revenue by the end of 2026 (Financial Times)
headline_summary: Anthropic targets October IPO at $2T+ valuation, $100B revenue
blurb: Anthropic is heading to IPO in October at a valuation exceeding $2 trillion, a figure that surpasses SpaceX's previous private valuation record. The AI startup expects to generate $100 billion to $120 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026. This IPO reshapes how venture capital allocates globally and confirms that the AI sector has reached true mega-scale commercial maturity.

title: Mirae Asset to inject additional $35 million into Korbit crypto exchange following July acquisition: report
headline_summary: Mirae Asset injects $35M into Korbit after $91.5M acquisition
blurb: Mirae Asset is deploying an additional $35 million into Korbit crypto exchange following its initial acquisition. The South Korean asset manager acquired 97.15% of the platform for $91.5 million in July, securing majority control. The follow-on capital demonstrates traditional asset managers now treat crypto exchange infrastructure as ongoing investments requiring sustained funding, signaling strategic institutional interest beyond one-time transactional acquisitions.

title: Goldman Sachs to gain bitcoin and ETH income ETFs in up to $2.25 billion Neos acquisition
headline_summary: Goldman Sachs to acquire Neos for $2.25B in crypto income ETFs
blurb: Goldman Sachs is acquiring crypto fintech Neos Investments for up to $2.25 billion, gaining Bitcoin High Income ETF, Boosted Bitcoin High Income ETF, and Ethereum High Income ETF. Neos serves institutional and wealth-management clients seeking structured cryptocurrency yield. Tier-one finance houses' systematic acquisitions of crypto-native fintechs signal durable institutional capital reallocation into digital assets, fundamentally distinguishing this adoption cycle from earlier retail-speculation waves.

title: Anthropic Tries to Shore Up Investor Confidence Ahead of Blockbuster IPO
headline_summary: Anthropic Shores Up Investor Confidence Ahead of Blockbuster IPO
blurb: Anthropic is working to build investor confidence ahead of a blockbuster IPO, actively managing relations with its shareholders. The generative AI company's approach to the public markets signals the sector has matured enough for massive exits. For the venture community, this represents a major milestone: the first mega-cap AI IPO and proof that LLM companies can scale to public-market valuations.

title: Electric joins Databricks to bring WASM Postgres to AI agent sandboxes
headline_summary: Databricks acquires Electric to power AI agent database sandboxes
blurb: Databricks acquired Electric, which builds WebAssembly-based Postgres engines for AI agent sandboxes. The technology safely isolates database workloads in secure virtual machines without traditional performance penalties. As enterprises now deploy autonomous agents into production environments, they need reliable data access locked inside trustworthy security boundaries that can't be compromised. Databricks is betting sandboxed Postgres shifts from optional feature to essential infrastructure.
